Here is how it goes....

Dev writes games, using DX11 or whatever version API they use, also in this case the Gameworks API layer that interfaces with DirectX and the driver.

Game is broken.

Nvidia looks at game source, and says oh look, your code is broken here fix this it will work on our hardware, via.

Nvidia tests game, oh we can further optimize the game here, puts in optimizations in driver for particular game. Hence why display drivers have swelled over the years to 350 MB plus.

AMD says hey let me look at game source, Dev says sure here you go, however you can only look at 80% of the source the other 20% that calls Gameworks API which in turn calls the DX API and Driver is proprietary.

AMD says ok we did the best we could, however some things will still run like ass because the proprietary API that calls Driver/Direct X we have no idea how it handles the calls to the API so we can not properly optimize it..

We'll try some optimizations in driver, however since we do not know how Gameworks handles calls to Direct X and to our driver we can not do much.

Essentially AMD is not going to reverse engineer gameworks just so it can play nice with their drivers. Time is money and these companies do not pay the manufacturers to optimize their games. If Nvidia released the code to AMD they could easily optimize the gameworks API for their product. Unfortunately that is not the case.

I feel like its cheating, but I have to go with Transformers. All of them. I'm not someone that bores easily, but these films just bore me so much that I actually experience some minor physical manifestation of pain. Even during the action scenes, I'm helplessly and completely bored.

That's an extremely broad synopsis of Speaker for the Dead. And some of the details are completely wrong.
